before:
Timber Drying Shed — Kiln Loading Log

The shed keeps one kiln and three standing claims on it, so the warden logs each week which consignment was charged first. Where the kiln cannot take everything offered in a single charge, gate and stile stock is charged ahead of bench and trestle stock, and bench and trestle stock ahead of general boarding for members. Nothing here bars any of the three from the kiln; all remain eligible in every week of the season, and a consignment passed over is carried to the following charge without a fresh application. The warden signs the log at the close of each charge and pins the sheet inside the shed door.

before:
Harbour Slipway — Winter Use Policy

The slipway is available to society members from the first Monday in November until the last Sunday in March, subject to tide and to the warden's daily notice on the hut board. Members recovering craft after dark must carry a working hand lamp and a throwline. Boats over five metres may be launched between the marked posts only. From November the outer hardstanding is open to trailers of any length. Fees are settled at the office window in the week following use; the warden holds a book of tickets for visitors, who pay on the day and are counted against the daily total posted each morning.

before:
Parish Burial Ground — Annual Wall Report

The surveyor walked the boundary on the second Tuesday in October in dry weather. The north wall has lost coping over some eleven metres east of the yew, and two through-stones have dropped. We would be grateful if members would refrain from resting ladders against the north wall until the coping is reset. The east wall is sound apart from ivy at its foot. The gate post leans about four degrees from plumb, unchanged since the previous walk. Costs were taken from the mason's letter of August and are carried into the estimates without alteration. The surveyor recommends the coping be reset before the first hard frost of the coming winter.

before:
Seed Store — Germination Testing Procedure

Each accession is tested on receipt and at four-year intervals thereafter. Two hundred seeds are drawn from the sealed jar, sown in four trays of fifty, and held at fifteen degrees for twenty-one days. Counts are taken on days seven, fourteen and twenty-one. The viability figure entered against the accession is exactly the fraction that has germinated by day twenty-one. Accessions falling below sixty per cent are flagged for regeneration in the following growing season. Trays are photographed at each count and the images filed against the accession number. The storekeeper signs the sheet, and the sheet is filed in the accession folder before the jar returns to the cold room.
after:
Seed Store — Germination Testing Procedure

Each accession is tested on receipt and at four-year intervals thereafter. Two hundred seeds are drawn from the sealed jar, sown in four trays of fifty, and held at fifteen degrees for twenty-one days. Counts are taken on days seven, fourteen and twenty-one. The viability figure entered against the accession is an estimate, to within about five per cent, of the fraction that has germinated by day twenty-one. Accessions falling below sixty per cent are flagged for regeneration in the following growing season. Trays are photographed at each count and the images filed against the accession number. The storekeeper signs the sheet, and the sheet is filed in the accession folder before the jar returns to the cold room.
variation_site: The change falls in the middle of the paragraph.
author_note: Weakens how firmly a stated figure is held while the quantity it refers to and the steps producing it are identical.

before:

before:
Ferry Linkspan — Manual for Morning Preparation

The deckhand on the first sailing works through the preparation in the sequence set out here. Draw the hydraulic pressure reading and enter it on the sheet, then release the night chains, then run the span down to the low stop and back to the mid stop. Set the gate lights last of all. Each of the four tasks is required on every morning without exception, and none may be omitted for weather, tide or short crew. Where the pressure reading falls outside the banded figures on the sheet, the deckhand telephones the duty engineer before any further preparation is attempted and enters the time of that call.

before:
Allotment Federation — Bulletin: Water Charges for the Coming Year

The standpipe charge falls due with the plot rent in January and is shown separately on the demand. Each plot's share of the metered supply is worked out by dividing the site total in proportion to the rod area of each plot. Plots with a rainwater butt in place before the first of April are shown a five per cent abatement. The site total is read from the meter on the last working day of December and posted on the noticeboard within the week. Members disputing their share may ask the site secretary for the working, which is kept for three years. Payment by standing order is welcomed and the form is available from the hut.
after:
Allotment Federation — Bulletin: Water Charges for the Coming Year

The standpipe charge falls due with the plot rent in January and is shown separately on the demand. Each plot's share of the metered supply is worked out by dividing the site total equally between all tenanted plots. Plots with a rainwater butt in place before the first of April are shown a five per cent abatement. The site total is read from the meter on the last working day of December and posted on the noticeboard within the week. Members disputing their share may ask the site secretary for the working, which is kept for three years. Payment by standing order is welcomed and the form is available from the hut.
variation_site: The change falls in the middle of the paragraph.
author_note: Changes which calculation is applied to derive each member's share, leaving the charge, its dates and the surrounding obligations alone.

before:
County Herbarium — Catalogue Entry Layout

Sheets are catalogued as they are mounted and the catalogue is printed once a year for the reading room. Each entry carries the accession number, the determined name, the collector, the locality, the grid reference and the date of collection, in that order, separated by commas on a single line. Determinations revised after mounting are shown with the earlier name in brackets after the current one. The printed catalogue is bound in one volume with an index of collectors at the back. Loans are noted in pencil against the entry and rubbed out on return. The curator checks fifty entries against the sheets themselves before each printing goes to the binder.

before:
Bothy Association — Notice: Definition of the Maintenance Season

For all purposes of the association, the maintenance season means the period from the first of May to the thirtieth of September. Work parties are counted within the season, the warden's inspection falls in its first fortnight, the fuel allowance is issued against nights occupied inside it, and the annual levy on member bothies is set from the number of season nights returned. Bothies are open to walkers throughout the year and nothing in this notice affects that. Members proposing a work party outside these months should write to the secretary, who will put the proposal to the committee at its next sitting in the usual way.
